newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel January CPI +0.4 vs +0.8 in December.
newsitem.headline: Israel January CPI +0.4 vs +0.8 in December.

text.p: The Central Bureau of Statistics issued the following economic indicator on Friday:
ISRAEL CONSUMER PRICES Jan 97 Dec 96 Jan 96
Note: To compare previous indices based on 1987=100.0, multiply indices from January 1994 by 2.421.

The January index was slightly under estimates by government and private sector economists, who had forecast a rise of about 0.5 percent. The index was boosted by relatively high increases for home maintenance, health and miscellaneous factors.

The housing price index, regarded by economists as a key barometer of future inflation, rose 0.7 percent, slightly under estimates of 0.8 percent. The housing index had risen unexpectedly sharply in December, spurring concerns that home prices might begin exerting upward pressure on the CPI.
The wholesale price index rose 0.5 percent.

Analysts had said prior to the CPI's release today that the index would not be indicative of inflation in coming months because the inflationary effects of a strengthening dollar and higher produce prices would only be reflected in the February CPI.
The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange does not trade on Fridays, so there was no immediate market reaction to the CPI.
